_comment: The CLOSED capability registry (ADR-0562). The single machine-readable source of truth for the canonical capability set of the capability-first repo organization. Coarse / Conway-aligned: one capability per two-pizza ownership boundary. Seeded from ADR-0536's sixteen substrate domains + the verified current tree (cloud/ + oya/). A crate maps to EXACTLY ONE registered capability via the ADR-0562 deterministic placement rule; new top-level dirs outside this registry plus base/build/third-party/governance/kernel/os/app FAIL the membership lint. De-brand naming is realized via the ADR-0532/0533 profile mechanism; the names here are the de-branded canonical slugs (the flip is a later Phase-0 lane). This file is governance data; it now lives at its ADR-0562 §2 destined home governance/capability-registry.json (moved from specs/ 2026-08-14, the unblocked strangler item). DATA, not code: canonical-json governed, reachability-registered, council-architecture owned. CAPABILITY TIER FACETS (`tier` + `substrate_dag_position.stratum`, spelled exactly as in a service manifest.json per ADR-0245 tier-as-facet): a capability that carries them DECLARES its dependency tier here, beside its definition. cloud-ci-tier-dependency-acyclicity reads this and derives NOTHING — the tier was previously PROJECTED from each capability's absorbs_current_dirs, which resolved only while those service dirs still existed (a completed move orphaned the tier) and whose unanimity was computed over whichever services had not moved yet (migration ORDER decided the answer). An UNDECLARED capability is RED and non-baselineable in that gate the moment it enters capability_roots; there is deliberately no fallback, because a fallback covering for a missing declaration is how a silent exemption returns. NINE capabilities are deliberately undeclared, each needing a founder/architecture ruling rather than an invented value: marketplace SPANS tiers (product + substrate — the ADR-0562 "a single engine spans tiers via its faces" case, so it may need splitting rather than a tier); iam spans S1+S3 with three untiered absorbed services; storage, ci, billing and flags have only `forward-declared` evidence, which carries no ADR-0280 rank and so enforces nothing; policy, compute and messaging have no tier'd absorbed service at all. The fifteen declared values transcribe what every one of their absorbed services already unanimously declares.

meta_directories.charter: Rung-0 kernel floor; the recursion floor. Its own excluded/nested workspace per the ADR-0512 kernel carve-out. The kuberos no_std framekernel that formerly occupied this rung was retired by founder decision 2026-08-02 and deleted by commit c2ee2631a; the directory persists at rung 0 and holds the Asterinas evaluation as a black-box upstream pin.
cloud-os node operating system (Talos-class). The node substrate the capability ladder runs on.

Irreducible cross-capability primitives (Google //base). Admission rule: a crate enters base/ ONLY if depended-on by >=3 capabilities AND strictly below all of them in the ADR-0280 DAG. NOT a util/ junk-drawer.
Meta, off the runtime ladder: ADRs, specs, policy-as-data, this capability registry, the dep-lint authority, the masterplan.
Meta, off the runtime ladder: buck2 prelude, toolchains, reindeer, CI engines, and the generated sell-catalog (SKU/pricing) VIEW. Owns zero capability crates.

Meta, off the runtime ladder: reindeer-vendored third-party crate sources (the live buck2 cell root third-party//). TOP-LEVEL per the ADR-0615 amendment (founder 2026-07-10), split out of the build/ charter text. Owns zero first-party (capability) crates.
Composition ring: deployable surfaces wiring 2+ capabilities for a tenant (SaaS verticals + the web shell). app/<product>/ composes; it never defines a capability engine.

faces.charter: Capability traits; the stable seam. The lowest ADR-0280 DAG node the crate's public port belongs to is the tie-breaker for placement.
Transient-infra impls (adapter-aws/-oci/-capi); vanish at owned-stack cutover.
The multi-tenant surface we SELL (product face); depends on core/ ONLY through ports.

Integration-test-only crates carrying no production code. Admitted ONLY for the META directories whose runtime engines have no sold surface (kernel/, os/); landed precedent kernel/harness/asterinas-real-boot (ADR-0611) and os/harness/difftest-app (ADR-0562 §10.29). NOT a capability face: a capability keeps its tests beside the crate they exercise. Recorded here because the registry is closed and had been describing the tree inaccurately since ADR-0611 landed the first harness leaf.

capabilities.name: cell
capabilities.charter: Cellular topology substrate: cluster-per-cell, hard caps, thin static-stable cell router, autosharding/rebalancing. The leaf substrate (ADR-0280 bootstrap floor).

capabilities.name: iam
capabilities.charter: Identity: IdP (principals/credentials/passkeys), product-shared identity, consent(-graph), tenant-RBAC (role store/assignments), and workload-identity consumption. Produces the verified principal that the policy capability's PDP evaluates; the PBAC+ReBAC decision plane is the separate policy capability (ADR-0615). RBAC+ABAC identity facet.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: identity + oya-identity + consent(-graph) + tenant-rbac as sub-modules of iam (distinct core vs facade faces, not separate capabilities). RESOLVED (ADR-0615, founder 2026-07-10): the Cedar PDP / PBAC+ReBAC decision plane (policy) is EXTRACTED to its own standalone capability (ADR-0562 §7 split — OWNERS boundary axis-policy-engine + clean PDP port seam + this ADR amendment; ADR-0280 §D-13.D marks policy 'Standalone'). oya/policy + the policy-engine dag_node move to the policy capability; the Cedar PDP crates physically under iam/** stay iam-mapped to avoid a membership double-map. iam keeps identity/credentials/consent/tenant-RBAC/workload-identity consumption.

capabilities.name: policy
capabilities.charter: The Cedar-backed PBAC+ReBAC authorization decision plane (standalone, cell-distributed per ADR-0280 §D-13.D). G face: policy + ReBAC-tuple authoring/signing/distribution. C0 face: per-cell runtime PDP + last-known-good versioned tenant-policy/ReBAC snapshot store. Consumes iam identity (the verified principal); consumed by ~all capabilities' PEPs (gateway edge + every protected service). A stale snapshot denies or routes to the authoritative shard, never silently authorizes (static-stability invariant).
capabilities.boundary_note: EXTRACTED from iam (ADR-0615, founder 2026-07-10) as the 24th capability, reversing ADR-0562 §2's iam-absorbs-policy coarse collapse. ADR-0562 §7 split: OWNERS boundary (axis-policy-engine vs axis-identity) + clean port seam (the PDP consumes the iam principal; ~all consume the PDP) + this ADR amendment. Maps 1:1 to the pre-existing policy-engine DAG node (ADR-0280 §D-13; no DAG edit needed — the node and its identity/tenancy/cell + five consumer edges already exist). Only oya/policy moves; the Cedar PDP crates physically under iam/** stay iam-mapped (double-map avoidance). Precedent: AWS IAM vs Verified Permissions (Cedar, store-per-tenant); Google IAM vs Zanzibar (logically-global, physically-distributed-with-local-replicas). Not a singleton global PDP.

capabilities.name: tenancy
capabilities.charter: Tenant lifecycle + home-cell resolution + tenant-as-universal-scoping-primitive. The structural multi-tenancy substrate.

capabilities.name: secrets
capabilities.charter: KMS + secrets + workload identity (SPIFFE/SVID issuance). The crypto root (recursion break #1).
capabilities.boundary_note: KMS (key material) and secrets (secret material) share an OWNERS boundary and the crypto-root recursion break; kept coarse. Workload-identity SVID issuance (ADR-0553/0561) lives here as the issuance engine; consuming PEPs live in iam/.

capabilities.name: audit
capabilities.charter: Tamper-evident Merkle audit log; always-on, no kill switch. Seals the emitting principal + tenant scope.

capabilities.name: observability
capabilities.charter: Metrics/logs/traces/SLO substrate (ADR-0139 SLO-gated promotion). The agentic observability plane.

capabilities.name: data
capabilities.charter: Records + query engines: Spanner/Cockroach/RDS-class OLTP, BigQuery/Redshift/ClickHouse-class OLAP, Dataflow pipelines, ontology. No cloud-* crates. Not S3. Not web search. RAG is intelligence if sold.
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719: nested analytics/warehouse/pipeline/ontology/cloud-data dumps git rm. search-* purged (SERP is not RDS; RAG not strangler-moved). data-cloud-kernel/domain deleted — no cloud-* debt in this cap.

capabilities.name: storage
capabilities.charter: Durable bytes: object/CAS (S3/GCS analog). Not SQL, not Spanner/Cockroach, not BigQuery, not search.
capabilities.boundary_note: RESOLVED (ADR-0615, founder 2026-07-10): storage (substrate CAS/blob) vs data (ontology/OLTP) is a clean port seam. The landed storage/facade/{drive,recordings} domain crates (ADR-0562 §10.9) are CONFIRMED storage substrate product faces (single-capability, like the Q5 data facades); a future consumer Drive/Recordings product wiring storage+iam+comms+billing is app/. imaging (0 crates) awaits a later flat-product judgment (PACS); it is not an app/healthcare context. Its oya/imaging scaffold remains in this absorb until the storage Batch-5 move-plan can rehome it without orphaning. storage/facade also = the S3-analog CAS sold as infra (Amazon S3 the product, NOT ADR-0280 stratum S3 — the two spellings collide in this note). STRATUM (ADR-0631 floor test): the permitted range is S2..S5 — floor S2 from storage/core/domain -> cell/core/region (cell S2) and storage/facade/recordings -> comms/core/meet-domain (comms S2); nothing ranked consumes storage, so there is no ceiling. S2 is the FLOOR and is what is declared. The `tier_subtype: substrate-data` shared with cloud-data(S3)/ontology(S3) is NOT evidence for a mid-range S3: that subtype spans nine manifests which split 5x S3 (all data-capability services) and 4x forward-declared (cloud-storage, drive, recordings, imaging — precisely storage's own absorbs), so the subtype tracks the DATA capability's rank, not storage's. Declaring the floor also preserves headroom: every future ranked consumer of storage is legal at S2 and up.

capabilities.name: compute
capabilities.charter: Fleet orchestration (Borg analog): stripped Linux on Cloud Hypervisor (VM) and Firecracker (microVM/functions), plus our agent. Optional k8s-on-compute is a sold SKU facade, not how we operate.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse per founder ruling: compute is ONE engine (vm + k8s-on-compute + functions) with facade sub-surfaces, NOT three capabilities.

capabilities.name: k8s
capabilities.charter: Optional sold GKE/EKS-class SKU wrapping upstream kube (hosting, quota, SLA, CAPI). Not the fleet OS. Not a kubernetes.git port. Not Borg.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: owned control-plane (core) + managed-k8s (facade). The four managed-k8s-* dirs become facade sub-modules.

capabilities.name: network
capabilities.charter: Network + DNS substrate: service mesh, static-stable signed DNS snapshots, cell routing data plane.

capabilities.name: gateway
capabilities.charter: API gateway / SSOT edge: Check/Report enforcement point, public API contract surface, rate/quota enforcement.

capabilities.name: bus
capabilities.charter: Owned event/service bus (Pub/Sub + SQS analog + outbox). Kafka/Pulsar are adapters or a sold SKU facade, not core. Not notify (SES) and not mailbox/chat apps.
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719: capability is bus/. Path messaging/ is retired (git mv). Crate names messaging-* rename with KEEP+WORK, not as a live slug.

capabilities.name: intelligence
capabilities.charter: Managed inference + agent runtime (Vertex/Bedrock). Adapters to models, eval/proof, invoke facade. Not GuardDuty (detection purged ADR-0719). Not a chat app.
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719: intelligence/detection/ dump git rm. Detection is a later product, not this core. CLIs burned.

capabilities.name: workflow
capabilities.charter: Managed sagas (Step Functions / Cloud Workflows). Implementation purged ADR-0719 D-18; rewrite from proto/H3. Not the event bus (messaging). Not forms/tasks/SaaS.
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719 D-18: git rm of the n8n/SaaS/bus dump. Registry row kept as rewrite destination. No empty workflow/ scaffold.

capabilities.name: pipeline
capabilities.charter: Productized execute: graph+queue. Internal TAP (tenant #0) and sold Cloud Build are two facades. Workers run on compute/. Promotion graphs execute here; iac/ is desired state; k8s/ is the cluster. One required context presubmit. GHA/Tide/GateRun are not core. Not a JSON check product.
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse per founder ruling: ci absorbs cloud-ci + ci-controller + ci-tide + ci-webhook-gateway as sub-modules. STRATUM (ADR-0631 floor test): range S4..S5 — floor S4 from ci/facade/crate-name-prefix -> intelligence/core/cargo-prefix-domain (intelligence S4), no ranked consumer so no ceiling. S5 is picked over the S4 floor on independent corroboration: this capability's dag_node `delivery-fabric` is ALREADY forward-declared under substrate_dag_canonical_ordering.tier2_and_meta_forward_declared.S5_meta in specs/platform-architecture.json, authored without reference to this edge. Two sources that never saw each other agree.

capabilities.name: iac
capabilities.charter: Infrastructure-as-code substrate + GitOps reconciliation surfaces. Declarative state for the owned stack.

capabilities.name: billing
capabilities.charter: Metering + billing + pricing: three-clock accrual/rating/invoicing, tax, FinOps cost attribution. First-class sold-ness capability (NOT a product/ junk-drawer).
capabilities.boundary_note: Coarse collapse: metering + billing + tax + finops/cost as sub-modules. First-class cross-cutting sold-ness capability per founder ruling.

capabilities.name: marketplace
capabilities.charter: Signed plugins, Cedar install envelope, SKU engine. Sell-catalog VIEW is build/. Not KYC, escrow, payout, or developer portal (ADR-0719).
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719: developer-sdk/ and plugin-app-store/ dumps git rm. KYC/escrow/tax are payments/apps later. Engine is plugin-kernel + SKU, not a bazaar.

capabilities.name: compliance
capabilities.charter: Compliance + regulatory-evidence substrate: regulatory packs, data-class registry, DPIA/threat-model evidence, audit-pack generation. Governance-ENGINE surfaces are NOT here (see boundary_note + ADR-0615 §2 Q13).
capabilities.boundary_note: RESOLVED (ADR-0615, founder 2026-07-10): compliance (regulatory-evidence engine) and audit (always-on tamper-evident log substrate) stay SEPARATE across their clean port seam; compliance consumes audit. A collapse would need its own ADR amendment (ADR-0562 §7). NOTE (ADR-0615 §2 Q13): oya/governance does NOT belong in this absorb — it is 0-crate enforcement/policy residue that decomposes to governance/ (authority) + ci/gateway/cell (SLOs) + iac/ in the compliance/governance Batch-5 move-plan; this absorb entry is retained until that atomic move to avoid orphaning.

capabilities.name: notify
capabilities.charter: Transactional send (SES/SNS/FCM analog): email/SMS/push. Not mailbox, Meet, messenger, or contact-center (those are later app/). ADR-0719 D-18: comms/ dump purged; rewrite notify/.
capabilities.boundary_note: ADR-0719 D-18: ADR-0615 'comms substrate' is scoped-superseded. Collaboration products are apps. Cloud primitive is send-only. No empty comms/ scaffold.

capabilities.name: flags
capabilities.charter: Feature-flag / configuration substrate: dynamic config, progressive delivery, kill switches.

app_products_note: Deployable SaaS verticals (crm, hr, and the healthcare SKU/portfolio soft cluster of independent multi-month products [emr, pharmacy, patient-monitoring, healthcare-integration — not a single app/healthcare product or filesystem nest; emergency and imaging await later flat-product judgments], the SEPARATE app/health-diagnostics product [clinical lab, ADR-0615 §2 Q8], itsm, incident-management, payroll, treasury, payments, supply-chain-planning, production-planning, plant-maintenance, warehouse, real-estate, global-trade, learning-management, performance-management, quality-management, contract-lifecycle-management, financial-planning, marketing-automation, social [a separate app product, not a healthcare context], community, connect, docs/sheets/whiteboard/calendar/forms/design-collaboration, etc.) are app/<product>/ composition members under the placement rule, NOT capabilities. They wire 2+ capabilities for a tenant. Interview: office-suite retire (D41) for notes/slides/sites/office — retire-in-place, not app/; translate is an intelligence concern (D42). V1 keep products are hr/payroll/calendar/community (+ payments only after payments/ capability exists). The exact app/ roster is enumerated by membership_lint_coverage.app_products.current_dirs, not closed here; this registry closes the CAPABILITY axis only.
flagged_boundaries_resolved_by: ADR-0615 (founder 2026-07-10, Accepted) — the substrate/product split (ADR-0562 §3#5/§6: 2+ capabilities -> app/; single-capability sold surface -> facade). The product-boundary rulings are resolved: (1) storage-vs-data facades — drive/recordings CONFIRMED storage/facade, imaging -> a later flat imaging product (not an app/healthcare context); (2) console/ discarded (ADR-0719 D-16) — ops-dashboard pilot git rm, not a shell capability, not app/ops-console; (3) compliance vs audit — kept SEPARATE across the clean port seam; (4) comms substrate vs product — comms is the multi-channel SUBSTRATE, oya/emergency -> a later flat emergency product (not an app/healthcare context). The prior Phase-0 claim that intelligence/workflow/iac/tenancy dag_node reconciliation was fully populated is STALE: these dag_node values are target mappings, not proof of current graph membership. ADR-0635 graph v2 is a bounded slice spanning 11 of 24 capabilities; iac and 12 other capabilities remain omitted. Their exact face tuples and edges are DEFERRED to W0-C-TOPOLOGY-COVERAGE tracked by GitHub #1537 under the no-new-frozen-baseline rule. The per-capability boundary_note fields carry the durable rulings; structural absorbs->app_products relocations execute in each capability's Batch-5 move-plan (see pending_relocations).

pending_relocations._comment: ADR-0615-ruled absorbs->app_products relocations that await their capability's Batch-5 move-plan. The path is RETAINED in its current substrate absorb (to avoid orphaning against the membership lint) until the atomic move re-homes it. 0-crate scaffolds today.
pending_relocations.to: later flat imaging product (PACS; slug TBD, not an app/healthcare context)
later flat emergency product (ED clinical; slug TBD, not an app/healthcare context)

membership_lint_coverage._comment: ADR-0562 §6 membership-lint COVERAGE extension (Phase-0). The capabilities[].absorbs_current_dirs close the cloud/+oya/ SERVICE-dir axis; this block extends the closed registry to map EVERY remaining current crate (the cloud/oya app surfaces with no capability service-dir, plus the libs/ and tools/ crates that dissolve into capability homes + meta dirs per ADR-0562 §1, 'libs/ dissolves into capability homes + base/'). Each entry maps a PRE-MOVE current path → a registered capability slug OR a meta directory (kernel/os/base/governance/build/third-party/app). The membership lint reads these PRE-MOVE; POST-move the path itself is the namespace. Genuinely-ambiguous crates that the strangler must home per-crate are NOT force-mapped here — they live in frozen_unmapped_baseline and the gate enforces no-regression against that frozen set. DATA, not code.

app_products._comment: The cloud/+oya/ deployable SaaS verticals + the web/application shell that are app/<product>/ composition members (app_products_note made machine-readable). They wire 2+ capabilities for a tenant and define no capability engine. PRE-MOVE these live at oya/<product>/; POST-move at app/<product>/. V1 keep products are hr/payroll/calendar/community (+ payments only after payments/ capability exists). office-suite retire (D41) for notes/slides/sites/office — see retired_v1_products; do not absorb into app/. sheets stays here as the ontology/action-event-document product spine (D41 did not name it). workplace-integration is the 'etc.' catch-all surface in app_products_note. application is the developer application/web shell (product-developer-application-shell) → app/ (ADR-0719 D-16: not a console/ capability).

retired_v1_products._comment: Interview: office-suite retire (D41) — do not app-absorb notes, slides, sites, or office. translate is an intelligence concern (D42), not a product. Trees deleted this wave (reorg/d41-retire-notes-slides-sites-translate). current_dirs lists only live paths.
retired_v1_products.disposition: retire-in-place; do not absorb into app/; D41/D42

meta_directory_absorbs._comment: Rung-0 kernel floor (ADR-0512 carve-out). The kuberos framekernel that formerly occupied this rung was RETIRED by founder decision of 2026-08-02 (keep Asterinas, delete kuberos/cloud-kernel), executed by commit c2ee2631a on 2026-08-14; cloud/ now holds zero tracked files and cloud-kernel no longer exists. The bare `kernel` root is the ADR-0611 landed destination (kernel/core/asterinas-boundary + kernel/harness/asterinas-real-boot live there today, in kernel/'s own excluded nested workspace); it is absorbed exactly like every other destination root so the crates that already sit at the destination map to meta:kernel/ once the root is scanned.

absorbs_current_crate_globs._comment: The dep-lint / check authority + the governance kernels + the corpus substrate. ADR-0562 §1 names 'the dep-lint authority' as a governance/ resident; owns_crates:false on the meta dir means it owns no CAPABILITY crates, not that governance/ hosts no governance-engine code (consistent with build/'s 'Owns zero capability crates' wording). The libs/oya-check-* and libs/oya-governance-* crates ARE the dep-lint authority; ADR-0580's governance/corpus/* crates (corpus-core, corpus-extract) are the Phase -1 live-AST corpus substrate physically homed under governance/ — also governance-engine code, not a capability crate. The membership-lint glob is a stem starts_with match, so governance/corpus/* covers both leaves.

Off-runtime-ladder build/CI engines + buck2/workspace/manifest-generation tooling. ADR-0562 §1 build/ charter: 'buck2 prelude, toolchains, reindeer, third_party vendoring, CI engines'. The remaining tools/*-app crates are build/CI tooling, not capability engines.
The owned data plane primitives (ADR-0562 'data→data'): the data boundary/outbox/SQL kernels + adapters dissolve into the data capability home.

frozen_unmapped_baseline._comment: BORN-ADVISORY FROZEN BASELINE (ADR-0562 §6 strangler burn-down). These current crates are genuinely ambiguous PRE-MOVE — they are the libs/oya-shared-* cross-capability junk-drawer the reorg explicitly dissolves PER-CRATE (idempotency/outbox/pagination/pdp/scim/webauthn/etc. each home to a different capability or to base/ pending the >=3-consumer admission check), the libs/oya-http-* middleware (base/ candidates pending the ADR-0280 DAG admission verification), and other base/ candidates pending DAG admission. They are NOT force-mapped to a wrong capability. The membership lint is ADVISORY for these but enforces NO REGRESSION: no NEW crate may join this list, no NEW top-level dir may appear, and the list burns DOWN as the strangler moves home each crate. FLIP-TO-BLOCKING TRIGGER: when this list reaches size 0 (post-strangler), the lint promotes from born-advisory to blocking. Each entry is a current crate dir (repo-relative).
